## Module to write
path: ReplicatedStorage/NumberFormat.luau
purpose: Feature: Leaderboard: leaderstats show Cash and Rebirths for every player, and a big in-world leaderboard board stands in the central plaza (SurfaceGui on a themed stand, title 'TOP TYCOONS') listing the top 10 players in the server by lifetime earnings (a server-tracked TotalEarned value), refreshed every 5 seconds, each row showing rank, name, rebirths and formatted earnings (1.2K, 3.4M). Format all big numbers in the HUD the same way through a shared ReplicatedStorage NumberFormat module. Bump counter leaderboard_refresh. -- Pure shared module returning one table. NumberFormat.short(n) turns numbers into compact strings: below 1000 it gives an integer string, then 1.2K, 3.4M, 5.6B, 7.8T. It uses at most 1 decimal, drops a trailing '.0', handles negatives, nil and NaN as '0', and rounds without rolling over (999950 gives '1M', not '1000K'). NumberFormat.withCommas(n) is an optional helper. It has no side effects and uses no services. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: leaderboard_refresh.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code bug. Do not change game code in response. Retry the step.
- If the critic says a code path was never exercised in the playtest, fix the pacing or setup so the path actually runs (e.g. cheaper first purchase) instead of only adding more code.
- When the spec changes the flow (e.g. from auto-assign to claim), rewrite the entry script (Game.server) to require and wire the new modules, and delete the old flow's logic (slots, teleport on join). Updating only the new modules leaves the old behaviour running.
- After a redesign, check that every module is required by the entry script and that its init function is called. Unwired modules never run, and their counters never fire.

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

### Theme.luau (Always first in a UI file: palette, fonts, corner/stroke/gradient/shadow/tween/pop/punch helpers, Theme.screen() for a ScreenGui that scales on phones.)
```luau
-- Theme: palette, fonts and style helpers every other UI kit snippet uses. Paste it first, once per LocalScript.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Theme = {
	Ink = Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38), Cream = Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232),
	Primary = Color3.fromRGB(255, 196, 41), Good = Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92),
	Bad = Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64), Info = Color3.fromRGB(64, 170, 255), Gem = Color3.fromRGB(190, 92, 255),
	Header = Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy, Body = Enum.Font.FredokaOne, Stroke = 3, Radius = 12,
}

function Theme.corner(gui: GuiObject, r: number?)
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, r or Theme.Radius)
	c.Parent = gui
end

-- border=true outlines the box; default outlines the text glyphs (the chunky game look).
function Theme.stroke(gui: GuiObject, px: number?, color: Color3?, border: boolean?): UIStroke
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Thickness = px or Theme.Stroke
	s.Color = color or Theme.Ink
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = if border then Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border else Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	s.Parent = gui
	return s
end

function Theme.gradient(gui: GuiObject, base: Color3)
	local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	g.Rotation = 90
	g.Color = ColorSequence.new(base:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.35), base:Lerp(Color3.new(), 0.12))
	g.Parent = gui
end

-- Hard drop shadow behind gui (same parent, ZIndex - 1). Call after gui is parented.
function Theme.shadow(gui: GuiObject, px: number?): Frame
	local sh = Instance.new("Frame")
	sh.AnchorPoint, sh.Size = gui.AnchorPoint, gui.Size
	sh.Position = gui.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, px or 5)
	sh.BackgroundColor3, sh.BackgroundTransparency, sh.BorderSizePixel = Theme.Ink, 0.4, 0
	sh.ZIndex = gui.ZIndex - 1
	Theme.corner(sh)
	sh.Parent = gui.Parent
	return sh
end

function Theme.tween(inst: Instance, t: number, props: { [string]: any }, style: Enum.EasingStyle?): Tween
	local tw = TweenService:Create(inst, TweenInfo.new(t, style or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), props)
	tw:Play()
	return tw
end

local function juiceScale(gui: GuiObject): UIScale
	local s = gui:FindFirstChild("Juice") or Instance.new("UIScale")
	s.Name, s.Parent = "Juice", gui
	return s :: UIScale
end

function Theme.pop(gui: GuiObject, t: number?) -- appear: scale 0 -> 1 with Back overshoot
	local s = juiceScale(gui)
	s.Scale = 0
	Theme.tween(s, t or 0.3, { Scale = 1 }, Enum.EasingStyle.Back)
end

function Theme.punch(gui: GuiObject, amount: number?) -- react: 1.2 -> 1
	local s = juiceScale(gui)
	s.Scale = 1 + (amount or 0.2)
	Theme.tween(s, 0.25, { Scale = 1 }, Enum.EasingStyle.Back)
end

-- Design in 1280x720 offsets; the UIScale fits it to any screen, safe insets keep it off notches.
function Theme.screen(name: string, order: number?): ScreenGui
	local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	gui.Name, gui.ResetOnSpawn, gui.DisplayOrder = name, false, order or 0
	gui.ZIndexBehavior, gui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling, Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets
	local scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
	local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera or workspace:WaitForChild("Camera")
	local function fit()
		local v = cam.ViewportSize
		scale.Scale = math.clamp(math.min(v.X / 1280, v.Y / 720), 0.6, 1.4)
	end
	fit()
	cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(fit)
	scale.Parent = gui
	gui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
	return gui
end
```
### CurrencyCounter.luau (HUD pill for coins/gems/cash bound to a leaderstat; number ticks up and pops.)
```luau
-- CurrencyCounter: HUD pill (coins, gems, cash) whose number ticks up, pops and flashes on change. Bind to a leaderstat.
local function short(n: number): string -- 999 -> "999", 12500 -> "12.5K", 3400000 -> "3.4M"
	for _, u in { { 1e12, "T" }, { 1e9, "B" }, { 1e6, "M" }, { 1e4, "K" } } do
		if math.abs(n) >= u[1] then
			return (string.format("%.1f", n / u[1]):gsub("%.0$", "")) .. u[2]
		end
	end
	return tostring(math.floor(n))
end

local function currencyCounter(parent: Instance, icon: string, color: Color3, pos: UDim2, value: IntValue | NumberValue)
	local pill = Instance.new("Frame")
	pill.Size, pill.Position, pill.BackgroundColor3 = UDim2.fromOffset(220, 56), pos, color
	Theme.corner(pill, 28)
	Theme.gradient(pill, color)
	Theme.stroke(pill, 3, nil, true)
	pill.Parent = parent
	local ico = Instance.new("TextLabel") -- emoji or letter icon; no asset ids needed
	ico.Size, ico.Position, ico.BackgroundTransparency = UDim2.fromOffset(64, 64), UDim2.fromOffset(-14, -4), 1
	ico.Text, ico.TextScaled, ico.Font, ico.ZIndex = icon, true, Theme.Header, 3
	Theme.stroke(ico, 3)
	ico.Parent = pill
	local num = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	num.Size, num.Position, num.BackgroundTransparency = UDim2.new(1, -60, 1, -8), UDim2.fromOffset(52, 4), 1
	num.Font, num.TextScaled, num.TextColor3, num.ZIndex = Theme.Header, true, Theme.Cream, 3
	num.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	Theme.stroke(num, 3)
	num.Parent = pill
	local shown: number = value.Value
	num.Text = short(shown)
	local token = 0
	value.Changed:Connect(function(new: any)
		local from, to = shown, new :: number
		token += 1
		local my = token
		Theme.punch(pill, if to > from then 0.15 else 0.08)
		num.TextColor3 = if to >= from then Theme.Good else Theme.Bad
		task.spawn(function() -- tick the number up over ~0.4 s instead of jumping
			for i = 1, 12 do
				if my ~= token then return end
				shown = from + (to - from) * (i / 12)
				num.Text = short(shown)
				task.wait(0.033)
			end
			num.TextColor3 = Theme.Cream
		end)
	end)
	return pill
end
```
### ChunkyText.luau (Any TextLabel players must read: titles, labels, timers, status text.)
```luau
-- ChunkyText: big outlined game text (titles, numbers, labels). Use for any TextLabel players must read.
local function chunkyText(parent: Instance, text: string, size: UDim2, pos: UDim2, color: Color3?, header: boolean?): TextLabel
	local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	l.Text, l.Size, l.Position = text, size, pos
	l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	l.Font = if header then Theme.Header else Theme.Body
	l.TextColor3 = color or Theme.Cream
	l.TextScaled = true
	local cap = Instance.new("UITextSizeConstraint") -- TextScaled fills the box; cap it so it stays even
	cap.MinTextSize, cap.MaxTextSize = 14, 72
	cap.Parent = l
	Theme.stroke(l, if header then 4 else 3) -- the thick dark outline is what makes text read as "game"
	l.ZIndex = 3
	l.Parent = parent
	return l
end
```

```luau
--!strict
-- NumberFormat: pure shared helpers for compact number display (no services, no side effects).

local NumberFormat = {}

-- Ascending list of units.
local UNITS: { { any } } = {
	{ 1e3, "K" },
	{ 1e6, "M" },
	{ 1e9, "B" },
	{ 1e12, "T" },
}

local function roundTenth(x: number): number
	return math.floor(x * 10 + 0.5) / 10
end

local function trim(v: number): string
	local s = string.format("%.1f", v)
	s = s:gsub("%.0$", "")
	return s
end

-- 999 -> "999", 1234 -> "1.2K", 999950 -> "1M", 3400000 -> "3.4M"
function NumberFormat.short(n: any): string
	if type(n) ~= "number" or n ~= n then
		return "0"
	end
	local num: number = n
	if num == math.huge then
		return "∞"
	elseif num == -math.huge then
		return "-∞"
	end
	local neg = num < 0
	local a = math.abs(num)
	local sign = if neg then "-" else ""

	if a < 1000 then
		local r = math.floor(a + 0.5)
		if r < 1000 then
			if r == 0 then
				return "0"
			end
			return sign .. tostring(r)
		end
		a = 1000 -- 999.5+ rounds up into the K range
	end

	local idx = 1
	for i = 1, #UNITS do
		if a >= (UNITS[i][1] :: number) then
			idx = i
		end
	end

	local v = roundTenth(a / (UNITS[idx][1] :: number))
	if v >= 1000 and idx < #UNITS then
		idx += 1
		v = roundTenth(a / (UNITS[idx][1] :: number))
	end
	return sign .. trim(v) .. (UNITS[idx][2] :: string)
end

-- 1234567 -> "1,234,567"
function NumberFormat.withCommas(n: any): string
	if type(n) ~= "number" or n ~= n or n == math.huge or n == -math.huge then
		return "0"
	end
	local num: number = n
	local neg = num < 0
	local s = string.format("%.0f", math.abs(num))
	local out = s
	while true do
		local replaced, count = out:gsub("^(%d+)(%d%d%d)", "%1,%2")
		out = replaced
		if count == 0 then
			break
		end
	end
	if out == "0" then
		return "0"
	end
	return (if neg then "-" else "") .. out
end

return NumberFormat
```
